A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EcoAlign and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across the appendix reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results across five LVLMs and six datasets, component ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and qualitative response examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a full-inference cost and latency comparison and further Llama lookahead-ablation results.

M1.justification: The graph expansion, weakest-link safety rule, budget-adaptive rollouts, valuation equations, and Pareto-based path extraction remain unchanged. v2 clarifies self-evaluation and supplies prompt templates, without establishing a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMSafetyBench, MSSBench, SIUO, OCRBench, MathVista, and MMStar. The additional efficiency comparison and Llama ablation introduce no new datasets, tasks, populations, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates Best-of-N with N=5 and unbounded Graph of Thoughts alongside standard inference and EcoAlign. The original Table 2 comparator set—Base, CoT, CoD, and VLM-Guard—is retained unchanged.

E3.justification: Section A.1.1 adds a separate evaluation accounting for the entire search graph and all API input/output tokens using GPT-4o pricing, together with normalized latency. Existing benchmark settings are retained. Naming GPT-4o as the judge is newly disclosed information, not an established change of judge.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds Llama-3.2-11B-Vision results testing dynamic lookahead against Myopic Search and Fixed Horizon. The original safety-aggregation, cost-control, and hyperparameter analyses remain available; their detailed discussion is largely relocated to Section A.1.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting; Best-of-N's five candidates do not constitute uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports EcoAlign full-inference cost/latency of 31.9/16.4 versus GoT's 36.7/20.9, normalized according to the caption. Figure 8 adds Llama ablation scores. Table 2, the original cost-control table, and existing plots retain their results; the new accounting does not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit asymptotic latency assertion contrasting O(N) linear/tree reasoning with O(log N) graph aggregation, citing Graph of Thoughts. No derivation accompanies it. The existing mathematical definitions, optimization objectives, rollout equations, and Pareto reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about economically governed graph search balancing safety, utility, and cost. Replacing explicit model/dataset counts with 'various' does not establish a substantive change in claim scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale for self-evaluation based on discriminative capabilities exceeding generative capabilities. Section A.1.1 also newly interprets the deployment objective as expected cost per safe, useful outcome. Earlier ablation interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Section A.2 newly supplies extensive prompts for initialization, risk assessment, action estimation, execution, and final synthesis, including output formats and scoring instructions. v2 also identifies GPT-4o as the evaluation judge and documents full-process token accounting. This substantially expands reproducibility information absent from v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Graph of Thoughts, Judging LLM-as-a-Judge, OmniSafeBench-MM, and Strata-Sword, while removing citations including TUNI and PixCLIP. These update the graph-efficiency, self-evaluation, and safety context without substantially changing the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 is condensed into shorter summaries, with detailed ablation discussion reorganized into Section A.1.2. The appendix gains named experimental, prompt, and response-example sections. Author affiliations and localized wording change, while most of the main narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn; Table 3, Figure 8, and boxed prompt panels are added. The original cost-ablation Table 3 moves to the appendix as Table 4, and existing figures are repositioned. The original performance plots and response illustrations retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides substantial prompt documentation and a full-graph cost/latency comparison against search baselines, improving transparency and support for the efficiency claim. The gain remains limited by reporting ambiguities: Table 3 describes normalized latency while its accompanying text uses seconds, and the prompt gain/novelty scores are not clearly connected to the unchanged valuation equations.
